en: We do not consider those blessed who, through their skill in protecting a mere hundredth part of a corner of the earth, compose flatteries for petty kings agitated by the fire of uncontrollable pride;
rather, we resolve only to serve that Lord who, in the past, bestowed the status of the Lord of Wealth upon a ragged sage who offered him but a handful of grain. 1.
Is virtue not sufficient to restrain the belly? Is a handful of water not enough to satisfy the thirst for essence?
On the road, is there not a dustbin that requires no effort, and a tattered rag that needs no washing?
Alas! The wise indeed worship the belly-born from belly to belly in vain. ||2||
Let the digestive fire within the belly of Lord Śiva— filled with garlands of fierce flames that rival the splendor of the God of Love sporting in the lap of the ocean— blaze forth.
Yet, even as mere straw, we do not beg from the lords of the earth with words that exhale the fragrance of full-blown jasmine blossoms.
O Lord of the Wicked, this salutation with joined palms is offered to you as you sit upon the terrace outside the gate:
that my wealth—the ornament of Dhanañjaya’s chariot—is smokeless and possesses the luster of collyrium. 4.

Because it brings about service to the Lord until the fall of the body, this wealth—which extinguishes the fire of desire that has no other fuel—is true wealth; whereas other wealth merely increases greed. This is the wealth that lifted Govardhana Hill.
It is an excellent means of accomplishment, free from contradiction, and a perfect means of propitiating the wise. ||5||
There is nothing at all acquired by my father, nor has anything been acquired by me;
however, I possess on the summit of a mountain a treasure inherited from my grandfather.
Thus ends "The Five Verses on Dispassion" composed by Vedāntadeśika.
